title: A nine-event J0205+6449 catalog does not match the scope of a 13-event study from 2019
abstract: We audit a public glitch list before a size-based forecast test for PSR J0205+6449. The tested Jodrell Bank snapshot has nine events, all before the cutoff of a 2019 study that reports 13. Only one of four dates in a separate timing paper matches within the catalog date error plus one day. The difference can reflect missing entries, revisions, definitions, or source errors. A fit to four early listed intervals gives 58.1 percent more squared error than a constant on four later intervals. Nearby splits reverse the comparison. The sample and event mismatch do not permit rejection of a physical size-wait relation. No new event or source is found. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval steps are included. Raw records and papers remain outside the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Event counts have different source scopes. Forecast error gains change sign across nearby time splits. These tests do not establish a physical relation.

citations.reason: Published event count, cutoff and size-wait context.
Separate timing report with four calendar dates; observations may overlap.
Related time-split forecast method in a different pulsar. No code or records reused.
